newsitem.title: GERMANY: Britain's Howard rejects FBI-style Europol.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Howard rejects FBI-style Europol.

text.p: Britain's Home Secretary Michael Howard insisted on Tuesday that Europol, Europe's fledgling police agency, would never acquire the powers of an FBI-style force despite Franco-German efforts to expand its role.
He was speaking a day after French President Jacques Chirac and German Chancellor Helmut Kohl called for Europol to become an "effective police authority with operational powers".

Howard said after a meeting with German Interior Minister Manfred Kanther that Britain believed Europol's role should be to collate intelligence from European Union countries and to assist and advise national police forces.

"We don't see any role for Europol in setting up the kind of international police force which is going to start investigating crimes or arresting people within the territory of the member states," Howard said after his talks with Kanther.

He said his German counterpart had assured him the "operational powers" mentioned in Kohl and Chirac's statement following Monday's Franco-German summit did not mean Europol would acquire the sort of characteristics Britain opposed.

But senior members of the German government and other European leaders, such as Irish Prime Minister John Bruton, have called for the Hague-based agency to be turned into a European version of the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) with powers to carry out its own operations.
German Justice Minister Edzard Schmidt-Jortzig said as recently as Saturday Europol should become a fully-fledged police force.
"Europol should be in a position to coordinate investigations on international organised crime and to lead its own investigations in member states," he told the Welt daily.

Howard noted Britain on Tuesday became the first country to ratify the Europol Convention regulating the agency's operations, and insisted London was keen to see it succeed as a centre of advice and assistance for national police forces.
He also rejected Kohl and Chirac's call for more qualified majority voting among EU member states on internal security matters.

"We don't go along with that but my discussions today...have made it clear that common polices rather than communitisation are really the priority for the Germans, as indeed they are for us," Howard said.
